newsitem.title: USA: Seagate agrees to buy Quinta, to take charge.
newsitem.headline: Seagate agrees to buy Quinta, to take charge.

text.p: Seagate Technology Inc. said Wednesday it agreed to acquire the remainder of Quinta Corp. that it does not already own in a deal worth at least $230 million.
Quinta, which is based in San Jose, Calif., develops ultra-high capacity disc drive technologies.

Seagate, a leading data technology company, said it expected to post a charge of between $180 million and $215 million in the quarter in which the transaction closes to write off in-process research and development.
The company also said Quinta shareholders will be eligible to receive, upon the achievement of certain product development and early production milestones, additional payments of $95 million.
Seagate, based in Scotts Valley, Calif., currently holds a minority interest in Quinta.
Seagate said it entered into the deal to meet an anticipated increase in demand for affordable, high-capacity, on-line storage.
It said Quinta's new optically assisted Winchester techonology is capable of "substantially" increasing disc drive storage capacity.
Seagate's stock added 44 cents to $35.44 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
